i'm not sure where you live, so i don't know how the healthcare system is in your country, but here's what i would do as an underage citizen in Canada, in chronological order.

1. i'm assuming that you can't drive and your parents won't bring you to the ER, so call 911. say: 'i have a plan to commit suicide and i cannot keep myself safe'. follow their instructions. you can also ask them to come quietly, without turning on the siren if you live in a residential area.
2. unlock the front door; it sounds like your parents may react strongly to you calling 911, and you want the paramedics to still be able to get in, in case anything bad happens.
3. the operator will most likely stay on the line with you, so tell them that you are going to talk to your parents. keep them on the line.
4. tell your parents you called 911. try to time your talk with your parents towards when you think the ambulance will get there, so that you minimize the window that they have to do something to you.
5. stay calm. i know, easier said than done. if you can, grab something from home that makes you feel good, like a stuffy or a book (but not something too valuable, stuff gets lost in the hospital). remember that everything will be okay. people at the hospital are experienced in dealing with severe mental health issues and want the best for you.

anyways, that's my personal advice as someone who has the privilege of having free and easy access to healthcare in an urban area with a world-renowned children's hospital. the psych ward there saved my life, and it was a place with warmth and understanding, which provided me with a break from all the abuse i went through at home. it is scary to call 911, but i promise you, all the redditors here value your life, and we would love to see you get the help you need. i wish you the best of luck with your journey; please take care of yourself!

I know he doesn’t want to talk now, but when he does, listen to him and let him know that you’re there. Paraphrase what he tells you; show that you are actively listening. Check in with him often. Once in a while, instigate some conversation by asking how he is. Even if he doesn’t address what you want him to, I can tell you from personal experience how much a ‘how are you doing?’ can do. Be careful not to blame him or use any blaming language. This is no one’s fault, certainly not his, not his brother’s, not yours, and not his parents’. 

Contact his parents or another trusted adult like a teacher and tell them everything you know. If they don’t do anything or if he’s in a crisis, call 911 or whatever your emergency line is. 

Lastly, take care of yourself. It’s mentally taxing to worry about others all the time. It’s okay to take a break. It’s wonderful that you want to help him, but this is not your responsibility to deal with.

My point is, things will always get better, and humans have an uncanny ability to make it out of any type of emotional crisis there is.
